transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-01-31 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~48m
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood), Priya (Redwood SE), Marco (CSM), Marta (Northbridge MLOps), Samir (Platform), Olivia (Security), Ben (SRE)

Summary: quick weekly POC sync to confirm credentialing progress, runbook for rollforward, and plan a staging latency burst test. Some brief discussion about SSO attributes and KMS options.
Topics: credential handoff, SSO/SAML mapping, KV cache perf, rollforward playbook steps, security docs and audit logs
Action items gist: see action_items above

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining on the Friday sync, gonna do quick rundown of what we did this week and then jump into the gate checklist.
[00:20] Marta: yeah thanks, quick note, we made progress on the IAM roles, still blocked on one service account for the gateway, Ben is digging in, umm, Samir will coordinate with your infra slack channel.
[00:35] Ben: yeah i'm in there, i've got the service account creation script but need the exact scope for token vault, and also, small gotcha, our KMS team asked about HSM-backed keys which might affect connection flow.
[00:50] Priya: okay that's useful, HSM note logged. For the POC we can start with envelope encryption and then swap to HSM once SSO is green. We should document the key rotation expectations in the playbook.
[01:05] Samir: question on SSO, we have SAML with AzureAD, but the attributes they pass are kinda limited, can Redwood accept email + groups? we also want a subset role mapping.
[01:20] Jordan: yes we support SAML / SSO mapping, we usually map email and groups and then create RBAC entries in the console. i'll attach the SAML attribute mapping example. note the sample says group claim should be 'groups' but sometimes it's 'http://schemas.microsoft...' so there may be mismatch.
[01:40] Marta: that mismatch is the problem we've seen with other SaaS providers, if you can share the mapping example that'll help us avoid back-and-forth.
[01:50] Jordan: will do. Marco: do you want to cover the rollforward playbook?
[02:00] Marco: yeah quick pass — we propose a stepwise rollforward: 1) credential validation and smoke tests on staging, 2) run a targeted latency bench (kv-cache warm/cold), 3) gradual traffic ramp with auto-fallback to hosted model if latency > SLO, 4) post-cutover observability check and audit log export. we're thinking of a 3-phase window to limit blast radius.
[02:25] Olivia: audit log export is important for us — can you confirm logs include token-level trace and model variant used? we need that for compliance.
[02:40] Priya: yes, the console exposes per-request trace id and model name, also we can push logs to your SIEM via syslog or S3 export. note that the default retention in POC is short but we can extend for the test window.
[02:58] Olivia: good, we'll need a temporary retention extension for the staging run.
[03:05] Jordan: we'll add that to the checklist.
[03:12] Ben: re: KV cache perf — when you say KV-cache warm/cold what's the expectation for me to prepare? we have limited resources in staging, don't want to skew results.
[03:28] Priya: good question. For the latency burst we want two passes: first cold-start (empty cache) to measure worst-case p99, then warm pass after pre-seeding with a typical prefix distribution. I'll share a seed script. the run will record p50/p95/p99 and tokens per request so you can compare cost.
[03:50] Samir: can you explain token cost? we have some teams that worry about runaway billing with long docs.
[04:00] Priya: sure, token cost here means per-generated token and input tokens. We'll provide a sample calculation sheet; for the bench we focus on consistent prompt shape to normalize cost.
[04:12] Marta: timeline wise we need to finish SSO test and service account by next week if we want to do the latency run in two weeks. any blockers?
[04:22] Jordan: main blocker noted is KMS/HSM confirmation and SAML attribute mapping. Otherwise we can stage credentials.
[04:30] Olivia: about KMS, our security team requires HSM-backed keys for production but for POC we'll accept envelope encryption with KMS if we can prove the integration path. i can share the KMS contact and policy doc.
[04:45] Jordan: perfect. Marco: i want to cover the rollback/rollforward check — if the staging bench shows p99 > 1.2x of baseline what's the plan?
[04:58] Marco: our playbook suggests: pause, scale pool (add dedicated capacity if needed), switch to compatible quantized model variant for lower latency, or failover to Redwood hosted in-region as emergency fallback. We'll include decision thresholds in the doc.
[05:18] Ben: what do you mean by "quantized model variant" — is that something we need to prepare on our side?
[05:25] Priya: no, model variants are managed on Redwood side. We can recommend a quant profile (8-bit/4-bit); the only customer-side requirement is to accept a different model name in the routing policy if we enable fallback.
[05:40] Samir: what about data residency? for now staging is in our eu-west-1 account, but production needs eu-central. any limits on region?
[05:52] Jordan: we support region pinning; for POC we can run in eu-west-1, and production region move is doable, we just need to plan image/variant availability. I'll note region pin in the playbook.
[06:05] Marta: okay i'm going to run through our checklist now — SAML mapping ready? partially ready, service account: pending, KMS: pending, log retention: pending, test users created: yes.
[06:20] Jordan: great, we'll prioritize SAML mapping example and the credential checklist.
[06:26] [brief side conversation, inaudible]
[06:45] Jordan: Priya, can you walk through the exact bench steps you'd run so Ben can prepare staging?
[06:52] Priya: sure — step 0: create three test accounts, give them limited token budget, step 1: cold run with 100 synthetic reqs at QPS 2, record p50/p95/p99, step 2: seed KV cache with 500 prefixes, then run warm run with 200 reqs at QPS 5 for steady state. we'll capture model latency, token cost, and CPU/GPU utilization where available. also we'll run a failure mode where one GPU node is removed to test graceful degradation.
[07:30] Ben: that sounds doable but need docs for the seeding script and the exact request shapes.
[07:36] Priya: i'll share the script (link: https://redwood.test/playbooks/seed-script - placeholder) and a sample payload. note sample contains medical PII redacted.
[07:52] Samir: question — you mentioned fallback to hosted model. will that route traffic out of our VPC? privacy folks want to know.
[08:02] Jordan: yes fallback to hosted means traffic leaves your VPC to Redwood hosted endpoints; for POC we can request an NDA addendum, but it's not ideal for production for you. We can also set a policy to only failover to a private cluster in another region if that helps.
[08:20] Olivia: that's a no for production, but POC might accept it if we limit volumes and get logs. Confirm we'll have audit trail of requests.
[08:30] Priya: yes traces are available. we'll also redact user PII on our side for analytics export.
[08:40] Jordan: ok moving on — any legal/procurement notes? Marta: procurement needs the SOW for the pilots and pricing estimates. Jordan: i'll send a brief SOW and an example pricing sheet after the call.
[08:58] Marta: also small ask — can you include a contingency for re-trying on transient GPU OOMs? we've seen those on other runs.
[09:08] Priya: yes our runtime has graceful retry and batching adjustments; we'll include that in the runbook with thresholds where we increase batching window or reduce max sequence length.
[09:20] Ben: is there a config we need to set for KV cache eviction so we don't fill memory during seeding?
[09:28] Priya: we'll share recommended cache size and TTL settings. default is LRU with configurable TTL.
[09:36] Samir: another item — do you encrypt cache on disk? security wants to know.
[09:42] Jordan: yes at-rest encryption is supported; if you need HSM for keys, we can plug in your KMS.
[09:50] Olivia: can you confirm whether audit logs include the model prompt plaintext or only hashes? we need to check with legal.
[09:58] Marco: by default we store request metadata and truncated prompt preview; full prompt logging can be disabled or redacted for POC. i'll note that as an option.
[10:10] Marta: ok that covers security clarifications. any open blockers not covered?
[10:18] Ben: i need the exact scope for the service account. Samir: i'll get that to you in slack today.
[10:25] Jordan: perfect, last thing — let's time the bench: target run the week of 2026-02-09. Does that work?
[10:32] Marta: yup that's fine.
[10:36] Jordan: great. recap of next steps and action items — Jordan to send playbook and SAML example, Marco to add rollback thresholds to playbook, Priya to share seed script and bench plan, Olivia to share KMS contacts, Marta to validate staging accounts. We'll reconvene in one week for a checkpoint.
[10:55] Samir: quick note, we might also want a short private deep-dive with your infra SE on KMS and network flow, can we schedule that?
[11:05] Jordan: yes i'll set a 45-min deep-dive next week; Priya and Ben and Olivia included.
[11:12] Jordan: thanks everyone, see you next week.
[11:18] [meeting ends]

Notes about transcript: occasional word swaps and truncated words; some links and doc names are placeholders.
